> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9ff8154cf694c616de5d467b35af21e037de1509` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6a4a9fb460d50aab6a245a27a3810874adc631e9` — the merge of head `c483a00ecc316adc468f61952a558554e84c8efb` into base `9ff8154cf694c616de5d467b35af21e037de1509`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6a4a9fb460d50aab6a245a27a3810874adc631e9 && git checkout 6a4a9fb460d50aab6a245a27a3810874adc631e9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9ff8154cf694c616de5d467b35af21e037de1509 c483a00ecc316adc468f61952a558554e84c8efb && git checkout -B drift-repro 9ff8154cf694c616de5d467b35af21e037de1509 && git merge --no-ff c483a00ecc316adc468f61952a558554e84c8efb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9ff8154cf694c616de5d467b35af21e037de1509
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9ff8154cf694c616de5d467b35af21e037de1509` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `939accc94e44b7765ea07c4f8d887ac382500c29`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/query.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/projection-names-a-field.ts, packages/spec/src/data/projection-names-a-field.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/query.test.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.query-and-get-record-empty-projection-refused.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/get-record-id-projection.integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/builtin-node-form-zod-ledger.test.ts, packages/rest/src/data-empty-projection-count-door.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/empty-projection-door.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts (FindDataRequestSchema), packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts (the POST query door), packages/spec/src/automation/flow-node-config-refusals.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (registerFlow), packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts (the stored-flow pulls), packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts (registerAndSaveFlow), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts (servedExpand), packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts, packages/client/src/query-builder.ts, ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-node-config.ts, skills/objectstack-query/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md, docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, .changeset/26644-*, 26909-*, 26910-*, 26954-*, 27008-* (all read on `origin/main` `fbe344b3`; the diff read against its base `9dec0545`). The five `content/docs/references/**` pages and the root changeset are prose faces: read for ②, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, judged against the live tree.

1. **`QuerySchema.fields` (`BaseQuerySchema`, `query.zod.ts`) refuses `[]` and a blank or whitespace-only member — right.** On `main` it is `z.array(FieldNodeSchema).optional()`. The in-process engine already refuses `fields: []` at `find` / `findOne` (`empty-projection-door.ts`, #27008, landed as 9fa70b4a), reading its sentence off `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.fields`, which took the same `transportProjectionArray(FieldNodeSchema)` arm in #26954. The declaration now admits what the runtime serves. The blank-member refusal is stricter than the engine door (which judges only `length === 0`), but it is the arm every published sibling already carries (`EngineQueryOptionsSchema.fields`, `$select`, `select`, `GetDataRequestSchema.select`), so the QueryAST joins one rule rather than inventing a second.
2. **Every nested `expand` value, at any depth, refuses the same — right.** `QuerySchema` is `BaseQuerySchema` extended with `expand`, a lazy `z.record(z.string(), QuerySchema)`, so one declaration covers the top level and the recursion; `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.expand` is the same `z.record(z.string(), QuerySchema)`. The engine door walks `expand` at every depth with the same refusal. Pinned at depth one and two in the new test.
3. **`QueryWithTransportSchema` canonical `fields`, hence `FindDataRequestSchema.query.fields`, hence the REST `POST /data/:object/query` body — right, and it matches the `$select` answer.** `QueryWithTransportSchema` is `queryObjectFace()` (a cast of `QuerySchema` itself) extended with `QueryTransportParamsSchema`'s members, so `fields` is the very arm `$select`'s array arm is (`transportProjectionArray(FieldNodeSchema)`), the object parse refuses before the fold transform runs, and `crud-routes.ts` answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `fields[0].field` = `query.fields`, as it answers `query.$select` / `query.select` since #26909. Before this head the same body was refused one layer down by the normalizer (`400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, pinned in the old `REFUSED_POST` table). Refused before, refused now; only the code and the locating key move, and that is exactly the move #26909 made for `select`. The querystring spellings (`?fields=`, `?$select=`) never reach this arm and keep the normalizer's answer. One consequence the PR body's REST row does not name: a POST body whose `expand.rel.fields` is `[]` likewise moves from the engine door's `VALIDATION_ERROR` (served through `mapDataError`) to the body schema's `VALIDATION_FAILED` at `query.expand.rel.fields`. Right, but should be written down (see ④).
4. **The API contract's `list.input` (`contract.zod.ts`) and the driver tuple inputs (`driver.zod.ts` find / findOne / count / aggregate / stream) narrow with it — right.** Both embed `QuerySchema`. No runtime in the repository parses either (grep over `packages/**` outside spec finds no `QuerySchema.parse` and no `.input.parse` of these tuples; `TursoDriverSpec` parses a driver definition, not a query), so no served request changes; what narrows is the published declaration and the JSON Schema a generated client reads.
5. **`GetRecordConfigSchema.fields` refuses `[]` and a blank member — right.** On `main` it is `z.array(z.string()).optional()` while the executor (`crud-nodes.ts` 498–550) hands `cfg.fields` to `data.find` / `findOne` as written, where the engine refuses it. The narrowing reaches every door that judges a builtin config through `flowNodeConfigRefusals`: `FlowSchema.parse`, `defineFlow`, `defineStack` (`422 STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` at `flows.N.nodes.M.config.fields`, pinned), `os validate` / `compile`, the metadata save door, `AutomationEngine.registerFlow` (which parses first), and the executor's own `parseNodeConfig` at run. The old run-time pin is rewritten to the config refusal with the engine never asked; the engine door keeps its own pin in `packages/objectql/src/engine-empty-projection-refusal.test.ts`, so nothing is left unpinned at a lower layer.
6. **A stored `sys_metadata` flow carrying `fields: []` is refused at registration — right, and it is the established seam.** `registerFlow` throws the first refusal from `registrationChecks`; every pull in `plugin.ts` (boot pull 1387, cold-boot bind 2596, re-sync 2520, mutation follow 2743) catches, warns with `describeThrownForLog`, and (where the flow was not already held) records it through `recordFlowRefusal` (#23316), so the flow is readable as refused rather than silently absent. ADR-0087's 2026-07-31 addendum names `registerFlow` as the flow's own rehydration seam and the many protocol-18 `*-refused` semantic entries on flow nodes use exactly this path. The consequence for an upgrading deployment is stronger than the prose says, though: on 18.2.0 (the released line; #27008 and #26644 are unreleased) such a flow registered and ran, reading every column; after this head it does not register at all, so none of its nodes run and its triggers stay unbound until the row is edited. See ③ and ④.
7. **The designer form's `fields` gains `minItems: 1` (`crud-nodes.ts`) — right.** It mirrors the contract the way `limit` already mirrors its floor, and the form ledger test pins both sides. `ui/` declares no `fields` input for `get_record` (`flow-node-config.ts` 816: objectName, filter, limit, outputVariable), so no `ui/` change is owed.
8. **`PROJECTION_NAMES_NO_FIELD` and `transportProjectionArray` move from `data-engine.zod.ts` to the non-barrel `data/projection-names-a-field.ts` — right, no public surface changes.** The module imports only zod, so no cycle; `query.zod.ts` could not have read them from `data-engine.zod.ts`, which imports `query.zod.ts`. Nothing is added to `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts` (precedent: `filter-save-door-refusals.ts`). `Type Check · source gates` (the lane carrying `check:generated`, `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs`) is `success` on this head. The automation-to-data deep import has precedent (`flow-value-slot-template.ts` reads `../data/context-tokens.zod`), and `Lint · ESLint` is `success`.
9. **JSON Schema: `minItems: 1` and a non-blank `pattern` on each member; TS types unchanged (`string[]`).** Right. `json-schema.manifest/automation.json` and `authorable-surface/automation.json` list schema and key names only, so no regeneration beyond the five `.describe()`-rendered reference pages, which the diff regenerates.
10. **Census — is any in-repo producer newly refused?** None. Every non-test `fields: []` literal on `main` is something other than a projection: a screen descriptor (`screen-nodes.ts` 502), a CLI orphan report row, analytics result shapes, UI column lists. `ListView.tsx`'s `fields: []` is a column projection handed to `ObjectGrid`, and `data-objectstack` puts `fields` on the wire only when non-empty (GET list and export), so it never meets either schema. `QueryBuilder.select()` with no arguments does yield `fields: []`, but no in-repo caller invokes it bare, and that query was already refused at the REST door on `main` (#26644); `client.data.find({ select: [] })` is refused client-side since #26910. Every in-repo `expand` producer authors entries without `fields` (`setRecordExpander` writes `{}` per relation; `data-action-routes.ts` writes `{ object: rel }`; `servedExpand` only withholds nested `expand`; objectql's nested read appends `id` to a non-empty list). `examples/**` carries one `get_record` with a non-empty projection. The dev's census (one authored `fields: []`, in the #27161 test) holds.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec`: **minor** — right. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` takes at least `minor` on a package whose `src/**` the diff moves, and the diff moves `query.zod.ts`, `builtin-node-config.zod.ts`, `data-engine.zod.ts` and adds the module and the D3 entry.
- `@objectstack/service-automation`: **minor** — right by the same rule: `crud-nodes.ts` moves (the form's `minItems`), and the level follows the kind alone, not the size of the hunk.
- `@objectstack/rest`: no bump — right; only a test file moves, nothing publishes. `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: untouched.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and in the changeset, with the BREAKING banner, Before / Now / Unchanged and the remedy — right: two published declarations stop admitting a list naming no field; nothing is widened, no key moves. The arm is BREAKING, so the full dogfood is owed; the dev ran it green and `Dogfood Regression Gate` is `success` on this head.
- ADR-0087 disposition: exactly one marker, `registered query-and-get-record-empty-projection-refused`, naming an id that is new in the diff and resolves (`semantic/18.*`, discovered by `build-migration-registry.ts`'s directory walk, so no committed registry changes). `Check Changeset` is `success`; `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (where `check-empty-changeset` and `check-adr-0087-registration` run) is `success`.
- `Skills-docs: none` with its reason — verified: `skills/objectstack-query/SKILL.md` teaches `fields` and nested `expand` `fields` only as non-empty lists (the `expand` value row, the nested-expand example at 263–274); `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` teaches `get_record` without `fields`. `content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx` already says an empty list is refused.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none.
- Dev finding 1 (main moved past `9dacccf9`, "none touches a file in this diff"): **the sentence is inaccurate, the risk is not.** Measured on `9dacccf9..origin/main` (18 commits at read time): `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` — a file IN the diff — moved in three commits (8b1740aa 11:14Z, 14e9685f 11:56Z, 8d79bbd7 12:01Z), and `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` (the cited `FindDataRequestSchema`) moved with them. The hunks do not overlap the PR's (the main-side edits are the draft-provenance, form-view-type and translation rows, not the `FindDataRequest.query.fields` row at 899, nor `FindDataRequestSchema` at 2401); GitHub reports the PR mergeable; all three landed before the PR's CI run (12:23Z), which tests the merge ref and passed `Type Check · source gates`; the reference page is `merge=os-regen`, so the queue regenerates it. No action owed under §10 (merge `main` only on a conflict, a main-caused red or a queue removal), but the acceptance note should say what was measured.
- Dev finding 2 (`.changeset/26954-engine-projection-empty.md` still says `engine.find(object, { fields: [] })` reads every column): **answered in ④ as should-fix 1** — this PR's changeset is the right carrier for the correction.
- Human Minimum item 3 unchecked (no repo-wide `pnpm lint`): `Lint · ESLint` and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` are `success` on this head; nothing owed.
- **The PR head has moved.** At read time the PR's head is `4dbe7883` (12:26Z, `docs(data-modeling): say where each spelling of an empty projection is refused`, one file: `content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx`, a prose face). That push cancelled the `Lint & Type Check` and `CI` workflow runs on `939accc9`, so on this head the aggregate contexts read `Lint & Repo Gates: failure`, `TypeScript Type Check: failure`, `Test UI: failure` (each because a lane concluded `cancelled`, per their annotations), with `Build Core`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI` cancelled — no measured red, and nothing green either. The lanes that did conclude on `939accc9` are all `success`: `Type Check · source gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards`. On `4dbe7883` the same lanes plus `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Test UI`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps` are `success`, with `Test Core`, `Build Core`, the `Type Check ·` lanes and the UI builds still running. The narrowing diff is byte-identical on both heads outside the prose faces, so this judgment carries to `4dbe7883`; the queue guard reads the newest record naming the PR's CURRENT head, so a record on `4dbe7883` is what lands it.

### ④ Design judgment

**Does the narrowing take a declared capability away at the consumer?** No. On `main` neither declaration says an empty list reads every column: `QuerySchema.fields` is described as "Fields to retrieve — names of the queried object's OWN columns", `GetRecordConfigSchema.fields` as "only these fields are read (default: all)", where the default is the absent key. "`[]` reads every column" was never declared; it was the driver's behaviour for an empty list, which #26644 (the REST doors), #26909 and #26954 (the transport and engine-side declarations) and #27008 (the engine entry, top level and every `expand` depth) ruled a silent widening and refused. The spec's own refusal was already real at the runtime; these were the last two published declarations still admitting a shape the runtime refuses, which is the card's symptom. The narrowing makes the declaration true, at the producer, which is where Prime Directive #12 wants it.

**Does the REST body refusal match the `$select` answer?** Yes, by construction and by pin — ① item 3.

**Is "no D2" honest for stored flows whose `get_record` node has `fields: []`?** Honest under the standing rule, and the right disposition; the prose around it is anchored to the wrong baseline. The only mechanical rewrite of `fields: []` is to drop the key, which reads every column — on 18.2.0 that is what such a flow did, so a D2 would be lossless against the released behaviour. But that mapping encodes "an empty projection means every column" into the permanent chain, which is precisely the silent widening #27008 refused for in-process callers ("got owner, organization and audit columns back, and was not told"), and the card's own Expected is that such a node is refused at save. Whether a stored `[]` meant "all" or was a list that came out empty is an intent no artifact records, which is the test `wait-node-event-config-required` applied to land D3-only in the same major. The D3 entry's `acceptanceCriteria` correctly sends the author to sweep stored `sys_metadata` flow rows as well as metadata files, and it is right that `os migrate meta --stored` cannot repair this. What the entry and the changeset get wrong is the "Before": "saved clean and failed at its first run" describes `main` between #27161 and this head, a state no release carried. The reader of the 18.3.0 upgrade guide arrives from 18.2.0, where the node saved, registered and ran, reading every column, and where `POST /data/:object/query` with `fields: []` answered 200 (the normalizer refusal, #26644, is in the same unreleased batch). And the registration consequence is understated: the stored flow is not "refused where a flow is registered" and otherwise left alone — it is left unregistered by every pull (`recordFlowRefusal`, a warn), so its triggers and schedules do not bind until the row is edited.

Tried to break it:
- Import cycle through the new module: none (it imports zod only; `query.zod.ts` and `data-engine.zod.ts` import it; `data-engine.zod.ts` still imports `query.zod.ts`). `BaseQuerySchema` is a load-time `z.object`, and `FieldNodeSchema` (368) is declared above it (514), so the arm is built from a live binding.
- `FieldNodeSchema`'s custom error map for the retired object form survives `.regex()` (zod clones the string schema with its checks and error map); `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.fields` has used this construction since #26954.
- The fold: `fields: []` is refused at the object parse, before `foldQueryTransportBag`, so the refusal names `query.fields` and never a folded key; `$select: []` beside it would be refused on its own member the same way.
- The `(narrowing)` arm with a `registered` marker on a change the runtime already enforced: `registered` requires a new id that resolves, which holds; `no-migration-prescription` would be refused because the body prescribes a rewrite (name the fields or drop the key).
- `check:generated`: the manifest and authorable-surface shards record names and keys, not constraints; only the `.describe()`-rendered pages were stale, and they are regenerated.

Findings:

- **Should-fix 1 — this PR's changeset should supersede the stale #26954 sentence.** `.changeset/26954-engine-projection-empty.md` ("`engine.find(object, { fields: [] })` still reads every column, as before") was made false by #27008, whose own changeset is in `@objectstack/objectql`'s CHANGELOG, not spec's, and carries no supersede. The foreign-changeset rule (#17712, `check-empty-changeset.mjs`) forbids editing the base file, so the 18.3.0 `@objectstack/spec` CHANGELOG would print "still reads every column" (#26954) and "the in-process engine already refuses it" (this entry) with nothing linking them. This PR's spec changeset is the one spec-package entry in the release on this exact rule; add the repo's "**Supersedes, in the same release:**" paragraph (precedent `25923-calendar-gantt-flat-fallback-retired.md`, and spec CHANGELOG 18.x `user-field-foreign-reference`) naming that file's "Unchanged" sentence and saying `engine.find` / `findOne` refuse it since #27008.
